 One of The Terminal List 's biggest stars is about to take on a different kind of role. The actor will star in an upcoming movie inspired by the downfall of a once-successful Wall Street trader whose life completely unraveled after he lost his job. The project also boasts an impressive ensemble, including an Oscar-winning legend.

 Following his work in Prime Video's The Terminal List franchise (including its prequel series Dark Wolf ), Taylor Kitsch is tackling the story of a businessman whose desperate attempts to conceal his financial troubles put his family and freedom at risk. The crime thriller will be directed by Matthew Gentile, who previously helmed American Murderer .
 Kitsch is set to lead The Long Island Bank Robber alongside Hollywood icon Christopher Walken and The White Lotus star Alexandra Daddario, according to Deadline . Kitsch will play Stephen Trantel, a former Wall Street commodities trader who, after losing his job, resorts to robbing banks and keep this a secret from his family. The Long Island Bank Robber goes to market next week for distribution and will begin filming in New Jersey this month.

 This isn't the first time Kitsch has taken on a morally complicated figure. He starred as cult leader David Koresh in the miniseries Waco and a troubled police officer in the second season of HBO's True Detective . More recently, he appeared as Ben Edwards in The Terminal List and Dark Wolf .

 Trantel's story attracted national attention in the early 2000s, when he was revealed to be responsible for a string of robberies across Long Island. His downfall provides the foundation for a thriller that will touch on desperation and the consequences of maintaining a double life. The movie is also adapted from 'Til Heist Do Us Part by authors Jeanne Callahan and Michael Harvey. Callahan is Trantel's real-life ex-wife and recounts the story from her perspective in the book.
 Gentile emphasized that the heist movie will explore deeper themes behind the true story and praised the star-studded cast behind it:
 " The Long Island Bank Robber is a true story I learned about in my youth, growing up in New York City as a true-crime obsessive. A propulsive heist film on the surface, the story also tackles complex themes of grief, survival, and marriage. With Taylor, Alexandra, and Christopher as our three leads — I could not have dreamed of a better cast to bring this film to life."
 While the bank robberies will be central to The Long Island Bank Robber , Gentile's comments suggest the film will spend just as much time examining the personal fallout of Trantel's actions. With Callahan's firsthand account as source material , the thriller has an opportunity to show how his double life truly affected the family he kept in the dark.
